messages.text: I’ll read the packet evidence and reconcile the active contracts, source hashes, and V5 protocol before issuing the gate status.

The dated acceptance matches the exact proposal hash. I’m checking the new plan against that boundary, especially whether V5 can prove rendered contrast across the required states and whether async ownership stays safe through replacement and disposal.

All 781 packet files match the frozen manifest. The raw-before files also match; I’m now reconciling the 543 current source entries against their origin and examining the bridge’s paint and acknowledgement lifecycle.

The source reconciliation confirms exactly two planning-only changes and 541 matches to origin. I also found a lifecycle conflict to resolve: the plan requires restoration on release, but the existing service releases prepared handles after successful publication while retaining the painted presentation. I’m checking the remaining V5 controls and state coverage.

V5 has a concrete coverage blocker: it permits opacity 1 or 0.65, while the unchanged vendor rule gives enabled pressed buttons opacity 0.75. The accepted scope preserves that opacity and requires active-state evidence, so V5 cannot certify that state as written.

The async failure path also needs clarification: after PAINTED, the parent accepts only the existing lower-menu diagnostic; an upper-glyph digest failure has no defined observable handling.
